settings.caption: TEJAS · Tay-jas · Saffron Collection
settings.title: TEJAS — Saffron Collection
settings.meaning: Inner Radiance · Luminous Vitality · The Fire of Transformation
settings.body_text: Tejas is one of the three subtle essences in Ayurvedic philosophy, alongside Prana and Ojas — it governs the luster of skin, clarity of eyes, and the glow that comes from internal balance. Directly associated with saffron's brightening properties in classical texts.
settings.desc: "The subtle fire that illuminates from within — the living light no highlighter can replicate. Kashmir saffron, rarer than gold, in two formulations that don't add glow. They uncover it."
settings.bundle_save_text: Purity · Radiance · The inner fire that illuminates from within

settings.caption: SHUDDHI · Shoo-ddhi · Rose Collection
settings.title: SHUDDHI — Rose Collection
settings.body_text: In Ayurveda, Shuddhi refers to the purification of the body and mind — removing ama (toxins) to restore natural radiance. Shuddhi Kriyas are the classical cleansing practices. The ritual before all rituals.
settings.desc: Before radiance, there is clarity. Rose cleanses. Rose restores. The skin remembers what it was before the world touched it."
settings.bundle_save_text: Purity · Cleansing · The skin remembers what it was before the world touched it

settings.caption: DINACHARYA · Dee-na-char-ya · AM Ritual
settings.title: DINACHARYA — Morning Ritual
settings.body_text: Dina = day, Charya = conduct. Dinacharya is a foundational concept in Ayurveda — the prescribed morning routine that Charaka Samhita dedicates entire chapters to. The most authentically Ayurvedic name of the seven.
settings.desc: "5,000 years ago, Ayurvedic physicians prescribed a morning ritual before everything else. Three products. Four minutes. The foundation your skin holds all day."

settings.caption: SWAPNA · Swahp-na · PM Ritual
settings.title: SWAPNA — Nighttime Ritual
settings.body_text: In Ayurveda, Swapna is one of the three pillars of health alongside Ahara (food) and Brahmacharya (conduct). Quality sleep is considered the greatest rejuvenator — nidra is when the body performs its deepest repair.
settings.desc: "In Ayurveda, night is not rest — it is repair. Cleanse the day. Feed the night. Wake to skin that worked while you slept."

settings.caption: ABHYANGA · Ab-hyan-ga · Weekly Spa Ceremony
settings.title: ABHYANGA — Weekly Spa Ritual
settings.meaning: Sacred Self-Anointing · The Ritual of Presence
settings.body_text: Abhi = toward, Anga = body. Abhyanga is prescribed in Ashtanga Hridayam as a weekly practice — applying warm oil with intention to nourish tissues, calm Vata, and honour the body as sacred. The most ritualistic name of the seven.
settings.desc: "The oldest beauty ritual in recorded history. Not skincare — a practice. Sunday's fifteen minutes that the skin holds for three days."
